purpose: Additional illustrative Flight Lab design variants; geometry, labels and data are not reference simulation outputs.

variants.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity 16:9 flat desktop screenshot of an alternative TensorAeroSpace Flight Lab design called 'Analysis workspace'. Scientific engineering software, calm LIGHT theme, warm white background, slate typography, thin neutral dividers, restrained cobalt-blue data lines and amber event markers, generous spacing, crisp readable English text. This is a new layout rather than a recolor of a dark cockpit. Header 'TensorAeroSpace / Flight Lab', tabs 'Analyze' 'Compare' 'Scenarios', small label 'Design concept'. Narrow left navigator: 'Runs', 'F-16 wingtip loss', 'AA-INDI', 'PID baseline', a compact list of channels 'Roll', 'Pitch', 'Airspeed', 'Applied input'. Center dominant data analysis area occupying 65 percent of width: three spacious vertically aligned plots 'Roll tracking', 'Applied aileron', 'Tracking error' with simple blue actual and dashed gray reference curves, a clearly aligned amber dashed line at '20 s' across all plots, short legends. Upper-right 3D viewport inset: understated gray parametric F-16 above a clean perspective coordinate grid, visible small amber damaged wingtip, short cyan trajectory, caption '3D replay'. Beneath inset, readable telemetry cards 'Airspeed 200 m/s', 'Altitude 2500 m', 'Time 24.6 s', and event list '20.0 s · Wingtip loss'. A minimal bottom shared timeline and playback controls, buttons 'Export replay' and 'Export report'. Tiny footer 'Illustrative data'. Strong hierarchy and typographic accuracy, charts use units and evenly spaced time ticks, optional channels not cluttered. No mountain photography, neon, holograms, device mockup, military insignia, random microtext, claims of measured performance. Prioritize readable real app design for notebooks, research and publications.

Use case: ui-mockup. Produce a polished landscape 16:9 flat desktop app screenshot for a NEW TensorAeroSpace Flight Lab 'Controller comparison' workspace. Elegant dark navy technical interface, cobalt and orange run identifiers, thin borders, legible English typography, ample spacing, no neon effects. Top bar exact text 'TensorAeroSpace / Flight Lab', nav 'Replay' 'Compare' 'Scenarios', badge 'Design concept'. Directly underneath, a concise common protocol strip: 'F-16 nonlinear', 'Wingtip loss at 20 s', 'Seed 47', 'Same actuator limits'. Main upper half has TWO equal-sized 3D flight viewports side by side, both show the same gray single-engine F-16 above a neutral coordinate grid, synchronized camera angle, small highlighted wingtip. Left title 'Run A · PID' with blue thin route line, right title 'Run B · AA-INDI' with orange thin route line. Clear small 'Link cameras' toggle and 'Align by: Fault event' dropdown. Use illustrative trajectories of similar scale without suggesting a proven winner. Lower half has one large shared line plot 'Roll error comparison' overlaying BLUE Run A and ORANGE Run B, reference gray dotted zero line, an amber vertical event marker '20 s'; adjacent compact comparison table title 'Evaluation summary', columns 'Metric', 'Run A', 'Run B', rows 'Tracking RMSE', 'Control effort', 'Recovery time', 'Constraint violations', numeric cells use em dashes rather than invented performance scores. Persistent lower-right text 'Illustrative data · No measured ranking'. Design emphasizes fair comparison and shared protocol, distinct run colors across viewport labels, paths and charts, no badges declaring best, no battle imagery, no holograms, no device frame, no excessive tiny text. Make this feel like practical engineering analysis software.
